79290.subject: Hot air?
79290.body:
Editor's Digest 

Автор: Financial Times


Автор: Financial Times

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/hot-air-financial-times-l50zc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BnT71bt48QSqlfeQ6jla4yA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=1E8DXkYert8Is1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mu5u3w77~7u-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mu5u3w77-7u
  
Hello from the FT newsroom. How seriously should we take promises made by AI bosses to slow the development of the technology? People close to Anthropic and OpenAI say the companies, which are both preparing to raise billions of dollars in public listings, have little in place internally to implement their proposed new safety standards. Besides, self-regulation can only go so far and the US government has shown little interest in strengthening guardrails on the industry. Even if America’s AI labs manage to set aside their rivalry for the greater good, there is no guarantee that the US and China will do the same. As Donald Trump and Xi Jinping prepare to meet in Washington next week, the two powers appear at odds over how to manage AI’s threats. My choices this week America’s mega-donors are overwhelmingly backing Trump’s Republicans in this year’s race for Congress, according to FT analysis. Find out who is bankrolling the party’s election push and how their money is (or isn’t) being spent. (Free to read) For more than six months, Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has been entirely absent from public view. Regime officials say this is a necessary security precaution. But many Iranians view it differently. The London borough of Wandsworth blazed the trail that came to be known as Thatcherism, a political and economic philosophy defined above all by low taxes. But this week, the Conservative-run council brought that era to an end. Here’s why. Nuclear fusion start-ups are attracting record investments on their promise of abundant, cheap and clean energy. But some scientists think their timelines are far too optimistic. (Free to read) Many had feared that Donald Trump’s pick to run the Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, would bow down to the president’s demands for low borrowing costs. But less than four months into the job, Warsh has led the central bank to its first rate rise since 2023. In today’s uncertain hiring environment, many young people are looking to job-hopping as a strategic alternative to a job for life. But is it a good strategy? Thanks for reading, Roula Khalaf, FT editor Recommended newsletters for you White House Watch What Trump’s second term means for Washington, business and the world. 79283.body:
Crypto Biz Newsletter

Автор: Cointelegraph


Автор: Cointelegraph

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/crypto-biz-clarity-act-setback-puts-coinbase-spotlight-4bktc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BsrXIR4F0Rv%2BO4R%2B2DMiKvQ%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=3FVgL6872L8Is1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mu5so0tg~wa-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mu5so0tg-wa
  
The crypto industry spent much of the past two years preparing for regulatory clarity in Washington. This week, one of its biggest legislative priorities hit a major roadblock. The CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate on Tuesday, falling short of the 60 votes needed to bring the bill to the floor for debate. The setback significantly narrows the bill’s path this year, with the Senate calendar tightening ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections. Strategists say crypto exchanges such as Coinbase may have more at stake than most from the stalled legislation. Elsewhere, Standard Chartered is betting big on Arbitrum, Bitmine is turning its Ether treasury into a source of staking revenue, and Phemex’s CEO says AI has been a “net negative” for crypto. Coinbase faces greater CLARITY Act fallout, Saxo strategist says Saxo Bank strategist Ruben Dalfovo said Coinbase has more at stake in the CLARITY Act setback because its trading business is directly exposed to US market-structure rules. In a Wednesday note following the bill’s failed procedural vote, Dalfovo said Coinbase is particularly exposed because new rules could determine registration requirements, tradable assets and who can participate on its platform. The setback could also affect other crypto-linked companies, though Dalfovo said their businesses are less directly tied to market-structure rules. Circle’s exposure is tied more closely to USDC adoption and reserve interest, while Strategy relies primarily on its Bitcoin holdings and access to financing. The market reaction reflected those concerns. Coinbase, Circle and Strategy shares fell between 5% and 10% after the vote and continued lower the following day. Continue Reading… Standard Chartered sees Arbitrum hitting $10 as Wall Street moves onchain Standard Chartered sees Arbitrum outperforming Bitcoin and Ether through 2030, driven by traditional finance firms moving assets onchain and transforming the network’s economics. Geoff Kendrick, Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets research, said Arbitrum receives 10% of net protocol revenue from companies building on it. Robinhood Chain, launched in July, has materially changed Arbitrum’s economics, with September revenue expected at $5 million, over five times the prior level. Kendrick projects ARB at $10 by 2030, a 70-fold increase from current prices around $0

79271.subject: 🟪 NEWS: Blockworks introduces Agentic Detection
79271.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/38f19638-14d6-4f17-8f68-5ae4d2eedf64/Agentic-Detection-202609d_Website_Article-Image-02.jpg?t=1789614735)
Caption: 



Customers of [Blockworks Monitoring](https://blockworks.com/products/monitoring) can now receive real-time alerts the moment our agents identify them, without waiting for an analyst to review. Customers get immediate visibility into a wider range of activity across the assets they follow.

When an exchange lists an asset, it takes on a responsibility that extends far beyond launch day. A security incident can demand an immediate response. A token migration can require coordination across the business. Keeping up with that activity across hundreds of assets takes constant attention, and even a team with endless resources will miss key updates.

Agentic Detection closes that gap. Within seconds of an event, it tells you what happened, which assets or organizations are involved, and where the information came from. Before an alert reaches your team, Monitoring filters the source material, connects related reporting, and organizes the findings with the original sources attached, so you can examine the evidence yourself.

Until now, every alert needed analyst approval before it reached customers. Analysts had to prioritize what they reviewed, and updates took minutes instead of seconds. Agentic Detection makes our findings available immediately.

Our mission at Blockworks is to build trust in onchain markets. For the exchanges, brokerages, and institutions supporting these markets, that trust depends on work that continues long after an asset is listed. Agentic Detection gives teams a wider view of those assets and more time to respond as they change.

To see how Monitoring can support your team, [contact Blockworks for a demo](https://blockworks.com/contact).

_P.S. To learn more, read our _[_launch announcement._](https://blockworks.com/insights/introducing-agentic-detection-asset-monitoring-built-for-the-ai-era)
